data.narrative:
Standard Electron is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Tyler Norwood and Alex Le Roux that has raised approximately $3.2M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though a narrow set of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers suitable for direct comparison is not available.

The valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology given the lack of sufficient same-stage comparables. Using total capital raised ($3.2M) as a proxy for Seed-stage value and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $8M. Peer-median analysis was not applied; while 8 same-sector companies exist (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix), none satisfied minimum thresholds for stage, proximity, or valuation-tier alignment necessary for reliable triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $7M (low) to $9M (high), with a median point of $8M. This range reflects uncertainty inherent in applying stage-based multiples to an early-stage company without robust peer anchoring. Key limitations include reliance on a single methodology and the absence of established Climate & Energy Seed-stage comparables. Future rounds and market conditions in the broader energy transition sector will materially affect valuation trajectories.
